claims.text: A_GWB = 2.4 (+0.7/-0.6) e-15 at f_ref = 1/yr, median and 90% credible interval, hd model with gamma fixed to 13/3, 14 frequencies
claims.product_needed: posterior chain of the hd13/3 model
claims.status_rule: No published product in the repository samples hd with gamma fixed to 13/3 (only varied-gamma chains). The Figure 1 data are on Google Drive, which is off limits. C1 as stated is therefore NOT TESTED. Exploratory estimate E1 below does not enter the verdict.
claims.tolerance: would be: each of median, q05, q95 rounds to the printed value at 0.1e-15, i.e. median in [2.35, 2.45)e-15, q05 in [1.75, 1.85)e-15, q95 in [3.05, 3.15)e-15

claims.text: Conditional posterior of log10 A at gamma = 13/3 taken from the varied-gamma HD chain hd_14f_pl_vg.core
claims.reasoning: With independent priors p(log10A) p(gamma) and gamma ~ U[0,7], p(log10A | gamma=g0, d) is exactly the posterior of the fixed-gamma model with the same log10A prior. The prior upper bounds differ (-14 for gamma=13/3 in Table 1 vs -11 or the code default for varied), but A ~ 10^-14.6 at gamma=13/3, so truncation at -14 should be negligible; checked by reporting the fraction of conditional samples above -14. The paper says gamma=13/3 sits at the 99% boundary, so few samples will be near it, and A and gamma are strongly correlated, so a raw window biases A.
claims.method_primary: samples with |gamma - 13/3| < 0.15; fit log10A = a + b (gamma - 13/3) by least squares within the window; adjusted log10A_i = log10A_i - b (gamma_i - 13/3); report median, 5%, 95% of 10**adjusted. Chain as loaded by la_forge core.Core(corepath=...) with its default burn, as the authors' notebook loads it.
claims.sensitivity: raw window (no adjustment) at half-widths 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20; adjusted at 0.10 and 0.20; extra 25% burn-in; bootstrap (2000 resamples, seed 20231108) of the primary estimate's median
claims.band: consistent if median in [2.2, 2.6]e-15 and q05 in [1.6, 2.0]e-15 and q95 in [2.9, 3.3]e-15 (rounding band widened by 0.15-0.2e-15 for slice Monte Carlo error)
